q: Is "Why this matters" pinned on the canvas or a side panel?
opts: pinned card top left; right-hand panel; header strip.
rec: pinned card docked in the intent band's empty left side (covers no label or node), collapsible, collapsed by default under 1100 px. It stays in view while panning and keeps the inspector free.
follows: SuperPlane (floating panels on the canvas).

q: Edge labels always on or on hover?
opts: all always; band-crossing always and in-band on hover; all on hover.
rec: band-crossing always, in-band on hover, so 23 edges stay readable.
follows: SuperPlane (channel pills only where they mean something).

q: Show kind words with technical detail, such as "route · POST /api/links"?
opts: plain label only; label plus kind and technical detail in the caption.
rec: caption with kind and technical detail, since the people reading the map are developers and the detail tells two routes apart.
follows: SuperPlane (node subtitle).

q: What happens at 900 px wide?
opts: fit the whole map (62%, text under 11 px); keep 100% and pan; fit with a floor.
rec: fit with a 62% floor, summary card collapsed, the right edge pans.
follows: SuperPlane (default zoom fits the content, minimum zoom lets it pan).

q: Show conflicts between decisions on the map?
opts: a Conflict footer and a "conflicts" edge; a badge only; inspector only.
rec: footer plus a dashed edge, and the inspector links to Needs you. It is the item's main risk. The second decision is mockup-authored (data-gap context-conflicts); drop it if the API cannot serve conflicts.
follows: none (our addition).

q: Are the band-crossing edges served? Answered by the context lane: yes. LensesView.edges[] has the cross-band edges and bands.product.edges[] the in-product ones; no data-gap is marked on edges. Only the second decision, the conflict and the suggested revoke.ts link remain gaps.?
rec: Answered by the context lane: yes. LensesView.edges[] has the cross-band edges and bands.product.edges[] the in-product ones; no data-gap is marked on edges. Only the second decision, the conflict and the suggested revoke.ts link remain gaps.

q: Should `?item=<id>` show a different map?
opts: map per item; the Link expiry map for any id.
rec: the Link expiry map for any id, because sample.json has one map.
follows: lead's instruction.

q: Should the file map be a sub-view or live in the inspector?
rec: sub-view (Map | Files, hashes #filemap and #files); a tree needs width.
follows: Linear (full-width list views).

q: should the inbox use one list grouped by kind, or tabs per kind?
opts: grouped list; tabs.
rec: grouped list. Linear groups issues under sticky headers and keeps one scroll; the four kinds stay distinct through glyph, header word and kind word.
follows: Linear.

q: where do Approve and Send back live, in the card or in a fixed bar?
opts: inside the card; fixed bar under the request.
rec: fixed bar, so the keys A and D always have a visible target.
follows: HumanLayer (actions under the request, kbd chips).

q: what does A do when the request was not read to the end?
opts: approve at once; show "Approve?" and need a second A.
rec: show "Approve?".
follows: HumanLayer's confirming state.

q: is the reason required when sending back?
opts: required; optional.
rec: required, with the send button disabled until text exists.
follows: HumanLayer (deny needs a reason, Ctrl+Enter sends, Esc cancels).

q: is "Edit before approve" built?
opts: drawn only; wired; left out.
rec: drawn and marked "our addition" until the API can approve with changed output. HumanLayer has no such action.

q: should stop 1 show answered questions, since none are open?
opts: show them with the chosen option marked; hide the section.
rec: show them, so the owner sees what they decided. No reference app has this; closest is SuperPlane's run inspector showing inputs next to outputs.

q: how long does the 2-hour hand-back nudge stay?
opts: until dismissed; 5 seconds.
rec: until dismissed, because it asks for an action. HumanLayer's toasts expire after 5 s but only inform.

q: takeover clock figure, 1d 4h (brief) or 2h 50m (sample data)?
opts: either.
rec: 2h 50m, from `paused.timeoutLeftSeconds` and consistent with that step's 3 h limit.

q: show ids such as AC-1 to AC-3 next to the done-criteria?
opts: show them as small grey references; hide them.
rec: show them, small and grey, because people say "AC-2" when they send a scope back.
follows: Linear (identifier in mono tertiary at the start of a row).

q: what do people type to confirm a settings or workflow approval?
opts: the full action text (`approve profile 3f0c9a`); a short phrase (`approve 3f0c9a`).
rec: the short phrase, bound to the change's fingerprint. It keeps internal words off the screen and still stops a slip.
follows: the setup-once spec section 4 (typed confirmation).

q: does "Approve all new workflows" also open a typed field?
opts: hold button; typed field.
rec: hold button, 1.5 s, as the setup-once spec says for approve-all. The list above the button is the preview.

q: should the "Handed back" toast stay?
opts: stays; fades after 5 s.
rec: fades after 5 s, because it only informs. Mockup keeps it visible for review.
follows: HumanLayer toasts.

q: which words end a run, and in which tone?
opts: the four owner-approved words (DONE, FAILED, DIDN'T WORK OUT, CANCELLED), or reuse the old chip words.
rec: the four owner-approved words, in caps, 11 px/600; FAILED red, DONE green glyph, DIDN'T WORK OUT and CANCELLED neutral grey. The same word is used for the header badge, the runs sidebar card, the stage footer and the inspector badge.
follows: the owner's note, SuperPlane's footer tones.

q: runs for DIDN'T WORK OUT, CANCELLED and DONE do not exist in sample.json. Which items show them?
opts: invent clearly labelled sample runs, or leave the states unreachable.
rec: three sample runs (Export audit log ITM-01JR5, Rename saved views ITM-01JS2, Dark mode toggle ITM-01JK3), outlined as `data-gap="sample-end-states"`; the unresolved one follows the real review loop (rounds used up, then the re-check still finds a problem, which routes to the line's "Stuck" end).
follows: SuperPlane, which shows one run per end state.

q: `?run=` for items with no mocked canvas (ITM-01JN2 at the scoping stop, ITM-01JP4 with you).?
opts: open the running canvas anyway, or open needs-you.html.
rec: in the runs sidebar these two cards link to needs-you.html (the stop view and #takeover); a `?run=` for them falls back to the running canvas.
follows: HumanLayer (an approval opens the approval card).

q: where does "Take over" lead?
opts: act in place, or open the takeover screen.
rec: link to needs-you.html#takeover, as the owner said; the clock pauses there.

q: "See its context" scope.?
opts: link to the item's map, or to the selected step.
rec: link to context.html?item=<item id> from every step, stage and failure (one place to look).
follows: Linear's "open the linked thing" row actions.

q: the state switcher in the header (Running, Failed, Didn't work out, Cancelled, Done).?
opts: keep it, or rely only on the runs sidebar.
rec: keep it as a mockup-only control, shown at 1500 px and wider (hidden below so the title fits); the runs sidebar switches the same states. SuperPlane has no such control.

q: edge labels now that engine confirms edges are (from, on, outcome, to) without plain labels.?
opts: show the raw outcome, or keep the mockup's plain labels.
rec: keep the plain labels (marked `recipe-edges`); the plain label table comes later and is a text lookup on the outcome.
follows: SuperPlane's channel pills (a short word per output).

q: open at the active stage at 100%, or fit the whole run like SuperPlane's 30 to 80%?
opts: active stage at 100%, or fit to screen.
rec: active stage at 100% with the stage card fully visible and its incoming edge and pill in view (step text at least 11 px); F fits the whole run.
follows: SuperPlane's run view (selected node in focus), keeps our 11 px floor.

q: end words in caps or sentence case?
opts: caps chips, or sentence case.
rec: sentence case everywhere ("Done", "Failed", "Didn't work out", "Cancelled", plus "Waiting for you", "You took over", "Paused, needs you"), the same as workflows.html.
follows: SuperPlane's badges.

q: how do runs with no hand-built canvas open?
opts: one generator from a short spec, or hand-built canvases for all 12.
rec: one generator (stages before the current one are finished, later ones not started), with all board runs by id; only the Saved search sharing and CSV import limits runs are hand-built because sample.json has their steps. Step timing for generated runs is not served, so finished steps say so.

q: do the six steps live on a first-run page or under Settings?
opts: a first-run page that disappears; the Settings page, always there.
rec: the Settings page. Home links to it until all six are done, and a new repo adds its rows again later.
follows: Linear (the onboarding checklist stays reachable from settings).

q: do finished steps collapse away?
opts: hide them; keep every row, collapsed, with its detail line.
rec: keep every row so you can see what Sindri did ("approved just now", "3,100 files").
follows: Linear's checklist, which keeps ticked rows.

q: is the whole workflow list shown before the hold?
opts: a scrolling box; the full list.
rec: the full list, because it is the preview you are approving.
follows: HumanLayer (the whole request shown before approve).

q: does the map step have a button?
opts: a promote button; none.
rec: none. The owner rule says the map builds itself, so the row only shows progress and a Retry on failure.
follows: SuperPlane's integration status rows (status only, action on failure).

q: where does the terminal alternative for Onyx go?
opts: inside the Onyx row; one line under the list.
rec: one line under the list, so the six rows stay about the app.
follows: Linear (secondary alternatives as quiet footnotes).

q: What does a single click on a card or row do?
opts: (a) open the run inspector; (b) go straight to the run canvas.
rec: (a). A click opens the 480 px inspector, a double-click or Enter on an open run goes to the canvas, and "Open run" is always there. Why: SuperPlane's board opens the task drawer on click and the canvas only from the automation link.
follows: SuperPlane.

q: Does the Needs you chip approve here?
opts: (a) link to Needs you; (b) approve inline.
rec: (a). The chip links to `needs-you.html`, where the full request is shown. Why: HumanLayer shows the whole request before any approve.
follows: HumanLayer.

q: Which address does a list row open for a child run (a scoping or design run)?
opts: (a) the child's own address; (b) the item's whole-run address.
rec: (a) for the canvas link of a list row, (b) for the inspector, which always shows the item's five stages. Why: the list shows each workflow run, the board shows one run per item.
follows: Linear (a row is one issue).

q: What does "Mine" mean without an owner field?
opts: runs that need you or that you took over; or wait for an owner field.
rec: needs you plus you took over, marked as a data gap. Why: SuperPlane's "My" filter has the same meaning of "assigned to me".
follows: SuperPlane.

q: Is there a Done lane card when nothing has finished?
opts: show an empty lane; hide the lane.
rec: show it empty. Why: SuperPlane keeps empty lanes with "Nothing here."
follows: SuperPlane.

q: One status word per card, or a status word plus a "Needs you" chip? (The brief says both.)?
opts: (a) status word only, and the word is the link; (b) word plus chip.
rec: (a). "Waiting for you" and "Paused, needs you" link to `needs-you.html#stop-<item>`; "Needs you" stays only as the filter. Why: rule 3 asks for one status word per thing.
follows: SuperPlane's board card (one status icon, one chip).

q: How many runs does the board show, and what is invented?
rec: 12 runs. Eight are invented to show every status and every lane (see notes); the four real ones come from the sample.
